title: Dutch controls reveal impact of hot weather on standards
summary:
Title: Dutch controls reveal impact of hot weather on standards

URL Source: https://www.foodsafetynews.com/2026/10/dutch-controls-reveal-impact-of-hot-weather-on-standards/

Published Time: 2026-10-05T04:01:53.000Z

Markdown Content:
Plus a warning on conditions for meat inspectors

![Image 1: Dutch controls reveal impact of hot weather on standards](https://storage.ghost.io/c/43/4e/434e508a-5e2f-4102-a53d-00bca10bb4bf/content/images/size/w30/2026/10/dreamstime_hamburger-food-service-fly-flies.jpg)

Published:October 05, 2026, 12:01 am

Food safety standards are often not met at hospitality venues, according to findings from a summer control campaign in the Netherlands.

The Dutch Food and Consumer Product Safety Authority (NVWA) said violations of food safety regulations were found at nearly two-thirds of inspected businesses.

Enforcement action was taken against 96 of the 154 companies inspected. This involved 88 official warnings and eight reports resulting in a fine. A follow-up inspection will take place within three months at non-compliant outlets.

Markdown Content:
The outbreak sickened people across 34 states

![Image 1: Salmonella outbreak traced to jalapeños has ended](https://storage.ghost.io/c/43/4e/434e508a-5e2f-4102-a53d-00bca10bb4bf/content/images/size/w30/2026/10/outbreak-map-jalapenos-10-02-26.png)

Published:October 02, 2026, 12:10 pm

## Subscribe to Food Safety News

Get the free version of our newsletter. No spam ever, unsubscribe anytime.

The CDC has called an end to the outbreak of Salmonella Javiana infections traced to imported jalapeño peppers.

A total of 488 people across 34 states were infected with the outbreak strain. There were 65 hospitalizations but no deaths, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. The patients ranged in age from less than 1 to 85 years old, with a median age of 31. Illnesses started on dates ranging from June 16 to Aug. 26, with the peak day being July 5 when 38 people fell.

There were likely many more sick people than reflected in the patient count. This is because some people do not seek medical treatment and others are not tested specifically for Salmonella. The CDC estimates for every confirmed patient in a Salmonella outbreak there are 29 who go undetected.

Traceback and epidemiological evidence showed that fresh jalapeños from Sinaloa, Mexico, and distributed by Coast Citrus Distributors were the source of the pathogen. The company recalled its whole peppers and its downstream customers who used the peppers in a variety of products [issued recalls](https://www.fda.gov/safety/major-product-recalls/2026-recalls-food-products-associated-fresh-jalapenos-sinaloa-mexico-and-distributed-coast-citrus?ref=foodsafetynews.com), according to the Food and Drug Administration.
